- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.10) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast dip by 5–10% relative to trend.
- If model shows sharp upward spike (e.g., >15% from prior 5-day avg), cap forecast at 1–2% above true peak to avoid overshoot.
- In low-sentiment environments (sentiment < -0.15 for 5+ days), model often underestimates mean reversion; add 2–5% upward bias to forecast tail.
- When sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (avg > 0.00), model tends to overestimate short-term volatility; smooth 30d forecast by 1–3% downward.
- If model forecast is >10% above true outcome for 3 consecutive days, apply downward correction of 1–2% per day to prevent overconfidence bias.
- In cases where true outcome deviates from model by >5% in first 5 days of forecast, adjust early days by 1–2% toward historical mean of last 10 days.
